title: Body drag re-spaces whole spline: moving a tail segment shifts the rest of the body
description:
## User Mandate
> "When I move one of the tail segments, it makes the rest of the body freak out"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Moving a tail body sample must NOT move the rest of the body (head/torso must stay put).
- Committed body DNA must remain valid: even chord spacing (DefinitionValidator `UnevenBodySpacing`), per the editor's authoring repair intent.
- Chosen direction (user confirmed): keep the committed body valid but re-space ONLY the free tail, leaving head/torso fixed. Rejected: dropping the auto re-space entirely.
- Local solver (`BodyEditSolver`, CC-016) already touches <= +-3 samples and must stay the local edit model. No competing DNA mutation or derivation path. No schema/serialization change.

## Summary
Reported bug: dragging a tail body sample makes the rest of the body deform ("freak out"). Root cause CONFIRMED: `CommitBodyDrag` (Assets/Scripts/Editor/CreatureEditorWindow.cs) writes the LOCAL `BodyEditSolver` output then, if `HasUnevenBodySpacing`, calls `BodySplineAuthoring.SpaceEvenly` on the WHOLE spline. SpaceEvenly is GLOBAL equal-chord resampling, so a local tail drag re-spaces every sample.

## Scope
- Replace the whole-spline `SpaceEvenly` commit-time repair in `CommitBodyDrag` with a repair that re-spaces only the free-tail side of the dragged sample, leaving head/torso samples fixed.
- Pure authoring math lives in `BodySplineAuthoring` (Editor assembly, no UnityEditor API), EditMode-testable.
- Add an EditMode regression test in `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/BodyEditSolverTests.cs` (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor) asserting distant samples never move on a tail drag while the committed spline stays even.
- Do NOT touch runtime generation, skeleton, appearance, or serialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A viewport drag on a tail body sample commits without moving samples on the head/torso side.
- The committed definition still passes `DefinitionValidator` even-spacing (no `UnevenBodySpacing` Error), or the design intentionally tolerates a documented bounded deviation only with user sign-off.
- Reproduced with the user's repro files Assets/Creatures/temp-bodysegmentmovebug-{pre,post}-9-6-26.json (only body.samples changed; post chords even, maxdev 0.00034 => SpaceEvenly ran; distant samples 6-27 moved up to ~0.021 model / ~0.0176 observed).
- EditMode test green; no regressions in ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor.

## Validation
- EditMode test in ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor (runs via MCP runner).
- Unity in-editor check on the user's dino: drag a tail sample, confirm head/torso samples unchanged and validation clean.
- Resolve head/tail convention in Unity before assuming which side is the free tail (code labels index 0 as "head"/Prepend and count-1 as "tail"/Append, which CONFLICTS with the tested appearance convention head = higher dot(pos, Forward); for Forward=+Z the head is the high index/#28).

## Findings
- `BodyEditSolver.SolveInteriorDrag` is local (<= +-3); on its own it moves 0 samples beyond that window.
- Spacing tolerance is ABSOLUTE 1e-3 vs the mean chord (GenerationTolerances.BodySpacingTolerance=1e-3f).
- `MutateDefinition` does NOT gate on validation errors (applies + revalidates + saves regardless).
- The commit-time global repair reintroduces the whole-body respace rolled back 2026-08-22, contradicting CC-016's stated "never re-spaces the whole spline; preserves existing samples."

## Blockers
- MemorySmith task tools were disabled for the first part of this session; now activated (this task exists).
- Full safe implementation needs iterative Unity validation (real editor behavior change, not a one-liner).

## Next Step
Implement the localized free-tail re-space helper in BodySplineAuthoring, wire CommitBodyDrag to it, add the EditMode regression test, and validate in Unity. Resolve head/tail orientation empirically first.
